title: Training resources for infectious disease modelling
text:
Note



This page is a curated resource list for students, PhD candidates, postdocs, and collaborators interested in infectious disease modelling, epidemiological statistics, mathematical epidemiology, stochastic epidemic models, model fitting, outbreak analytics, and network science.
Course dates, fees, eligibility rules, and application deadlines change frequently. Always check the official course page before applying. The selections and notes are personal and do not represent any affiliated institution.
Last manually checked: 2026-07-03
Maintainer: Fuminari Miura

title: Training resources for infectious disease modelling
text:
How to use this page
The resources below are grouped by training purpose rather than by institution. A practical learning route is:

start with epidemiological statistics and regression;
learn basic infectious disease modelling;
add mathematical epidemiology and stochastic epidemic models;
learn model fitting and inference;
specialize into network science, outbreak analytics, or agent-based modelling.

The labels in the notes are informal:







Label
Meaning




Core
Strongly relevant for infectious disease modelling training.


Recommended
Broadly useful for students or researchers.


Specialized
Highly useful for a specific modelling subfield.


Reference
Best used as self-study or supplementary material.


Archived / recurring
Past or recurring event worth tracking for future editions.

title: Training resources for infectious disease modelling
text:
Recommended training routes







Goal
Suggested route




Epidemiological regression from the basics
Imperial public-health R course → Nahhas regression book → WUR or Johns Hopkins regression/biostatistics


Basic infectious disease modelling
Imperial infectious disease modelling specialization → LSHTM introduction or FUN-MOOC → Keeling & Rohani


Mathematical epidemiology
Diekmann, Heesterbeek & Britton → ESPIDAM stochastic epidemic models → selected stochastic-process material


Stochastic epidemic models
Allen primer → branching-process / CTMC material → ESPIDAM stochastic epidemic models → LSHTM model fitting


Model fitting and inference
Statistical Rethinking → LSHTM model fitting and inference → Epiverse/outbreak analytics material


Network/contact modelling
Utrecht network science → ESPIDAM networks/contact patterns → EpiModel/SISMID network modelling

text:
Epidemiological statistics and regression



Resource
Provider / format
Level
Main topics
Notes




Statistical Analysis with R for Public Health
Imperial College London / Coursera
Beginner to intermediate
R, statistical thinking, linear regression, logistic regression, survival analysis, public-health datasets
Core. Good first course for epidemiological regression in R.


Biostatistics in Public Health
Johns Hopkins / Coursera
Beginner to intermediate
Biostatistics, regression, inference, public-health applications
Recommended. Useful for reading and conducting epidemiological analyses.


Multiple Regression Analysis in Public Health
Johns Hopkins / Coursera
Intermediate
Multiple linear regression, logistic regression, Cox regression, splines, adjustment, effect modification
Recommended. More focused regression course within the Johns Hopkins sequence.


Introduction to Regression Methods for Public Health Using R
Ryan Nahhas / online book
Beginner to intermediate
Linear, logistic, and survival regression; public-health examples; R implementation
Core reference. Good companion to any regression course.


Advanced Analytical Epidemiology
Wageningen University & Research / online course
Intermediate
Logistic regression, generalized linear models, mixed models, Cox models, confounding, effect modification
Recommended. Formal epidemiological analysis course in the Netherlands.


Statistical Modelling for Epidemiology
University of Edinburgh / online MSc module
Intermediate
Linear regression, logistic regression, survival analysis, diagnostics, model building
Recommended. Check whether single-course enrolment is possible.


Introductory Course in Epidemiology & Medical Statistics
LSHTM / short course
Beginner to intermediate
Epidemiology, medical statistics, regression, confounding, study design, infectious disease epidemiology
Recommended. Broad professional-training course.


Statistical Practice in Epidemiology using R
Bendix Carstensen and collaborators / short course
Intermediate
Logistic regression, Poisson regression, survival analysis, multistate models, causal inference, R
Specialized. Strong for classical epidemiological statistics in R.


Statistical Rethinking 2026
Richard McElreath / open course material
Intermediate to advanced
Bayesian regression, hierarchical models, causal models, posterior predictive checks, scientific modelling workflow
Core reference. Especially useful before Bayesian infectious disease model fitting.


GAM resources
Noam Ross / curated resources
Intermediate
Generalized additive models, mgcv, smooth terms, nonlinear effects, seasonality
Specialized. Useful for seasonality, humidity effects, nonlinear time trends, and surveillance models.

title: Training resources for infectious disease modelling
text:
Books, papers, and reference materials



Resource
Type
Level
Main topics
Notes




Mathematical Tools for Understanding Infectious Disease Dynamics
Textbook
Intermediate to advanced
Deterministic and stochastic infectious disease dynamics, \(R_0\), next-generation matrices, model formulation
Core. Main theoretical reference for mathematical epidemiology.


Modeling Infectious Diseases in Humans and Animals
Textbook
Intermediate
Epidemic models, heterogeneity, multi-pathogen and multi-host models, stochastic dynamics, spatial models, control
Core reference. Strong applied model catalogue.


A primer on stochastic epidemic models
Primer paper
Intermediate
CTMC, SDE, stochastic SIR, host-vector models, outbreak probability
Core reference. Short entry point to stochastic epidemic models.


A primer on the use of probability generating functions in infectious disease modeling
Tutorial paper
Intermediate
Probability generating functions, early outbreak, epidemic probability, final size
Specialized. Useful for branching-process and PGF intuition.


Introduction to statistical inference for infectious diseases
Tutorial / review
Intermediate to advanced
Stochastic epidemic inference, \(R_0\), final size, temporal data
Reference. Good overview of inference for stochastic epidemic models.


Stochastic epidemics in a homogeneous community
Lecture notes
Advanced
Stochastic compartmental epidemics, early phase, final size, law of large numbers, central limit theorem
Specialized. Mathematical treatment of stochastic epidemics.


Epidemic modelling: aspects where stochasticity matters
Perspective / short paper
Intermediate
When stochasticity matters, outbreak probability, early epidemic growth
Reference. Useful conceptual note on stochasticity in epidemic models.

title: Training resources for infectious disease modelling
text:
Maintenance notes
Suggested update cycle:

January: update spring and summer schools.
July: update autumn and winter courses, archive past events, and refresh deadlines.
Keep past events if they are recurring or useful as a future reference.
Prefer official course pages over secondary announcements.
Record a last_checked date whenever a major update is made.

Suggested status labels for future maintenance:



Status
Meaning




open
Currently accepting applications.


closed
Application deadline has passed, but the course may recur.


past
Event has passed and next edition is unknown.


self-paced
Available as online self-study material.


recurring
Offered repeatedly, often annually.


unknown
Status not recently checked.

title: About
text:
I am a Senior Researcher at the Dutch National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM), jointly appointed with Nagasaki University, Japan.
My work focuses on understanding how transmission processes unfold across heterogeneous populations and how epidemic theory can inform practical and timely control strategies.

title: CV
text:
Short Bio
Fumi Miura is a Senior researcher at the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM) in the Netherlands and is jointly affiliated with Nagasaki University in Japan. His research focuses on infectious disease modelling, with particular emphasis on transmission heterogeneity, contact networks, and the use of epidemiological and alternative non-epidemiological data to inform targeted intervention strategies.
